selected_result: Hallman–Ipsen Theorem 2.6: all-orders probabilistic forward-error bound for general summation trees

bibliographic_source.title: Deterministic and Probabilistic Error Bounds for Floating Point Summation Algorithms

paper_locations.anchor: Theorem 2.6; Algorithm 2.1 and Definition 2.1 on PDF pages 3–4; floating-point and independence models on PDF page 2

task_clarification: For n at least two, Algorithm 2.1 sums n exactly represented floating-point inputs by an arbitrary binary computational tree. Let h be that tree's height, defined as the longest downward path from its root to a leaf. Let s_k be the exact partial sum at internal node k and sHat_n the computed root result; s_n is the exact total sum.

Assume no overflow or underflow, the standard relative-error rule |delta_k|<=u for each of the n-1 internal additions, and Model 1.1: the local roundoff variables are independent and have mean zero. This is a conditional model, not an unconditional claim about every deterministic rounding execution.

For every delta and eta in (0,1), define lambda=sqrt(2*log(2*n/eta)). The event |sHat_n-s_n| <= u*exp(lambda*sqrt(h)*u)*sqrt(sum_{k=2}^n s_k^2)*sqrt(2*log(2/delta)) has probability at least 1-(delta+eta).
The internal exact sums s_k and h belong to the selected general summation tree, not the sequential prefix-sum vector.
scope_constraints: Preserve all general-tree evaluation orders; specializing to pairwise trees or sequential summation is partial coverage.
Preserve both failure parameters, the exact finite all-orders exponential coefficient, and the source's probability bound even when delta+eta exceeds one.
Do not assume the target event, concentration conclusion, or desired output-error bound as a field of the stochastic execution model.
